newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jerusalem mayor concerned by higher Arab growth.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem mayor concerned by higher Arab growth.

text.p: Israel's Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert said on Monday he was concerned by signs the city's Palestinian population was growing faster than the Jewish one.
Olmert spoke at a news conference where an Israeli research institute released population figures for Jerusalem, which the Jewish state views as its indivisible capital.
"The thing that concerns me more than anything else in these figures is the relative growth of the non-Jewish population in Jerusalem," Olmert told reporters.
The institute said the Arab population in the city was averaging growth of 4.5 percent a year while the Jewish population averaged growth of 1.3 percent a year.
The fate of Jerusalem, a religious magnet for Jews, Moslems and Christians, is one of the thorniest issues in the decades-old Arab-Israel conflict.
Palestinians view Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of their future state. Israel says it will never cede any part of the city.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem last March plunged Israel-PLO peacemaking into crisis.
The research institute said 603,000 people lived in Jerusalem, among them 422,300 Jews and 180,700 "Arabs and others".
It did not provide a population breakdown for each side of the city.
